newsitem.title: USA: US West Coast Lt. crudes lower, but ANS diffs firm.
newsitem.headline: US West Coast Lt. crudes lower, but ANS diffs firm.

text.p: U.S. West Coast light crudes remained below yesterday's levels, despite an increase in Alaskan crude prices following today's sale of a cargo by BP America, traders said.
The cargo, rumored at more than 300,000 barrels of Alaska North Slope (ANS) crude, sold at $1.30 below March West Texas Intermediate (WTI).
The buyer was a U.S. refiner in the Pacific Northwest, traders said.
Trade finished with ANS five cents a barrel higher at $22.60/22.80, as the tighter diff offset lower NYMEX prices.
Meanwhile, heavy California grades remained weaker in an oversupplied market, traders said.
Barrels moved east over the crowded All-American pipeline, or were offered to makers of heavy fuel oil, who must sell the product at a loss of about $2.00, traders claimed.
One trader said a major California producer sold about 100,000 barrels-per-day (bpd) at $1.00 under postings.
That compared with sales of 25 to 50 cents under postings.

Confirmed prices for San Joaquin Valley heavies ranged $17 to 17.25 a barrel Tuesday. So far, traders saw no major price shifts on lighter Valley grades, which are bought to pump heavies through pipelines.
